title: Edge-case stream retry coalescing and output sanity for hosted SSE
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several enterprise customers reported ongoing partial responses and truncated token streams during short network interruptions to the hosted SSE endpoint. Symptoms include: clients receiving a final 'end' event with incomplete structured output, resume attempts producing duplicated token fragments or gaps, and downstream consumers (runtimes using function-calling and structured schema validation) failing to parse or applying incorrect fallback logic. The problem appears correlated with our recent stream backpressure change that coalesces small in-flight packets at the edge router.
steps_to_reproduce: Start a hosted SSE generation with a long output (>2k tokens) and structured JSON schema enforcement.
Simulate a transient network glitch between 500ms and 3s (drop TCP segments or cut connection).
Allow client to reconnect using resume token protocol (client issues resume handshake with last-ack token offset).
Observe reassembled stream: check for duplicate token ranges, missing tokens in the middle, or immediate end events with truncated JSON object.
observed_behavior: Resume handshake sometimes accepts an offset that points inside a coalesced packet. The runtime returns suffix tokens starting at that offset but the edge router had already dropped boundary metadata, so the client receives duplicate token sequences or a token gap. In structured outputs this manifests as partial JSON objects or duplicate top-level fields.
expected_behavior: On transient disconnects clients should be able to resume from the last confirmed token with no duplication or missing tokens. Final 'end' events should only be emitted when the LLM runtime has completed generation and the entire structured payload validates against the schema. Resume protocol should be robust across router coalescing/backpressure behaviors.
root_cause_analysis:
Preliminary triage shows two interacting causes:
1) Edge router coalescing optimization batches small chunks into a single TCP payload and strips per-chunk metadata (sequence boundaries) to reduce overhead.
2) Resume token encoding relied on byte-offsets from the client-visible stream rather than an authoritative per-chunk generation sequence id. When a coalesced packet is sent, the resumed offset can resolve to the middle of an internal chunk leading the runtime to re-emit overlapping token ranges. Additionally, our hosted SSE early 'end' path triggers when the router signals FIN for the connection rather than confirming that runtime has flushed all chunked metadata, allowing a truncated final event to be delivered.
proposed_solution: Change resume token format to include authoritative generation sequence id + intra-chunk offset (immutable from runtime).
Restore per-chunk metadata preservation through the edge: ensure coalescing retains chunk boundary headers or inserts lightweight boundary markers that survive batching.
Modify hosted SSE 'end' emission path: require runtime acknowledgement of final chunk flush before emitting end event to client (idempotent end sequence).
Add server-side deduplication at the reconnection path: if overlapping token ranges detected by sequence id, suppress duplicates before forwarding to the client.
Add conservative default backpressure config for tenants with structured-output enabled; expose knob in Console to opt-in aggressive coalescing.
rollout_plan: Backend change (sequence-id resume token + dedupe): ship as runtime-1.18 feature flag behind 'sse-resume-v2' flag.
Edge router change (preserve boundary markers): staged rollout in two phases — internal datacenter canaries then 10% edge traffic for hosted API.
Telemetry & validation: enable verbose sequence-id logs for canary + synthetic alarms to check resume correctness on reconnections.
Gradual ramp: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 72 hours with rollback triggers based on error-rate and truncated-output metrics.
tests: Unit tests for resume token encode/decode with sequence id semantics.
Integration test harness to simulate edge coalescing and verify reassembly/deduplication behavior.
E2E contract test with structured JSON generation ensuring schema validation passes after reconnects.
Chaos test that introduces 0.5–3s TCP interrupts across synthetic clients to validate resume success rates >99.9%.
Perf benchmark to confirm coalescing preservation has <3% p99 latency impact for typical payloads.
monitoring_and_analytics: Dashboards: 'SSE Resume Success Rate' (by tenant, model, route).
Metric: 'sse.resume.duplicates' — counts of detected duplicate token ranges on reconnect.
Metric: 'sse.truncated_end' — events where client received an 'end' but payload failed schema validation.
Alert: resume_success_rate < 99% for top-10 tenants -> page oncall and pause rollout.
Saved query: sample request IDs for all reconnects in last 24h where duplicates > 0.
mitigation_and_workarounds: Temporary rollback of the aggressive coalescing optimization at the edge (immediate mitigation).
Customer-side workaround: increase client ack granularity (ack every 256 tokens instead of 1k) to reduce chance of mid-chunk resumes.
Enable structured-output tenant-specific throttling to force smaller chunks (via Console toggles) until full fix is live.
Support team script to run automatic reconstructions for impacted customers and re-emit corrected payloads from logs where possible.
